summary: Peter Fenner works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied under advisers Noble Ross Reat, Arvind Sharma, and Richard A. Hutch, as well as traditional teacher Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, and held a post at Deakin University.
Peter Gaeffke (1927–2005) was an Indologist and linguist. He held posts at Utrecht University (~1964–1975) and at the University of Pennsylvania, where he served as Professor from ~1975 to 1998.

Peter Gyallay-Pap works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He completed a PhD at the London School of Economics and Political Science in 1990 and was an adjunct at Adams State University, attested in 2007.

Peter Harvey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. He founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies in 1996 and served as Emeritus Professor of Buddhist Studies at the University of Sunderland (attested 2002–2015).
Peter Haskel is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He was a graduate student at Columbia University, where he studied under Yoshito S. Hakeda.

Peter James Gilks specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and the Australian National University (PhD attested 2010) under supervisor John Powers, alongside several traditional teachers.

Peter Koret works in Buddhist studies and linguistics. He completed his doctoral thesis at SOAS University of London and held posts at Arizona State University and the University of California, Berkeley.

Peter M. Scharf (born 1957) is an Indologist and linguist. He prepared his dissertation at the University of Pennsylvania under George Cardona, and also studied under Shree Narayan Mishra, Ludo Rocher, and Narendranath Pandey.
Peter Masefield works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied under supervisors L. P. N. Perera and Ninian Smart (attested 1986).

Peter Moran works in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at Tufts University and completed a PhD at the University of Washington under supervisor Charles F. Keyes, as well as with several academic and traditional teachers.

Peter N. Gregory (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Harvard University in 1981 and held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Smith College, and the Kuroda Institute.
Peter Schwabland is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his MA at the University of Washington under supervisor Leonard van der Kuijp.

Peter Schwieger (born 1952) is a scholar of Tibetology. He studied under Dieter Schuh (~1975–1981), succeeded Klaus Sagaster in 2001, and served as Professor at the University of Bonn from ~2002 to 2018.

Peter Skilling works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2004). He has held positions at Chulalongkorn University, École française d'Extrême-Orient, and the Fragile Palm Leaves Foundation.

Peter Stewart (born 1971) works in history, archaeology, and Indology. In 2011, he held posts at the Classical Art Research Centre and as Associate Professor of Classical Art and Archaeology at the University of Oxford (~2011).

Peter Zieme (born 1942) is a scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He held posts at the German Academy of Sciences (~1965–1991) and the Berlin-Brandenburg Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1992–2007).

Peter van der Veer (born 1953) works in religious studies, Indology, and sinology. After studying at Groningen and Utrecht, he held posts at Utrecht University, University of Amsterdam, and the Max Planck Institute (Director ~2009–2021).

Peter von Bohlen (1796–1840) was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Franz Bopp and Georg Wilhelm Freytag at Berlin and Bonn. In 1826, he became an außerordentlicher Professor at the University of Königsberg.

Peter von Bradke (1853–1897) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Dorpat, Tübingen, and Leipzig, completed his Habilitation at the University of Giessen in 1884, and held a post there from 1886 to 1896.

Petra Kieffer-Pülz is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied as a pupil under Heinz Bechert (attested 1996). She was a Research Fellow at the Academy of Sciences and Literature Mainz (attested 2013–2016).
